jas: Quick sync: we keep hitting ambiguity on active/active session affinity vs strict residency. Example: mobile client pinned to eu-west but failover routed to us-east and now legal flagged data residency breach.
kaito: Can you share the flow that caused the breach?
jas: Short: proxy saw node in eu-west slow → routed to fastest healthy region (us-east). No manifest check for tenant residency because the hint header was missing.
maya: Are we relying purely on client hints today? I thought we had server-side tenant residency metadata.
sophia: We do have tenant.residency metadata but it’s honored only during initial placement. Fallback routing uses latency-first policy.
jas: That mismatch is the bug. Two proposals: (A) resident-only leases: once a tenant is pinned to a resident region, fallbacks must stay resident-only unless explicit opt-in; (B) preflight routing: proxy checks tenant.manifest.residency and artifact.restrictions before cross-region forwarding; (C) client hint header `X-Region-Preferred` + `X-Redwood-Consent` that must be surfaced and logged.
kaito: (A) seems safest for compliance customers. But worst-case latency increases. We need SLO guardrails and an SLA-exceed path.
maya: For SLA-exceed, we can return a structured degraded response `{"code":"RESIDENCY_BLOCKED","message":"resident-only fallback suppressed"}` and surface link to tenant settings. Clients can opt-in to cross-region emergency failover.
sophia: Also add a fast operator escape: an emergency flag that SRE can flip to allow single-call cross-region for customer-requested incidents (requires legal audit).
ops-bot: ops-bot: proposal to add `residency_enforce_mode` feature flag (values: off, soft, strict) to proxy. soft = warn+telemetry+prefer resident, strict = block cross-region.
legal: legal: any change that allows cross-region transfer for resident-tenants must be logged with timestamp, operator id, and justification. We'll require an automated audit trail for opt-in.
kaito: Telemetry we'll need: `route.decision_reason`, `residency.blocked.count`, `residency.opt_in.count`, and traces that show preflight checks.
jas: Implementation plan: 1) add preflight check in proxy using tenant.residency + artifact.restrictions, 2) surface `X-Redwood-Degraded` header and JSON code as maya suggested, 3) feature flag rollout (soft->strict), 4) SRE operator escape with mandatory audit ticket, 5) update SDK docs for `X-Region-Preferred` and opt-in flow.
maya: Can we also add a lightweight client-side SDK helper that automatically sends consent when user toggles emergency-fallback in dashboard? reduces friction.
sophia: Good idea — but legal insisted consent must be explicit per incident. The SDK helper should open a consent modal.
jas: Timing: pilot soft mode in us-east next week, infra will emit telemetry. Kaito you own the RFC + small runbook. Legal please draft audit template.
legal: Will draft audit template and sample consent text.
kaito: RFC ETA: 48h. Will include manifest schema change `residency: {"region":"eu-west","enforced":true}` and proxy preflight pseudo-code snippet.
jas: Thanks all — pausing any automated cross-region failover for resident-tenants until the soft flag is live.
ops-bot: ops-bot: automated cross-region failover paused for tenant cohort `resident-*`.
